summary: The note describes poaching in aromatic liquors, a gentle cooking technique that infuses foods with spirits such as brandy, rum, calvados and bourbon, and is enjoying a resurgence as of autumn 2023. It draws on chefs, an instructor and a farmer who discuss temperature control, balancing aromatics, pairing with seasonal ingredients, and extending the method to proteins. It also notes sustainability benefits and the ritual of preparation.
one_line: Overview of poaching in aromatic liquors, covering technique, temperature, seasonal pairings, and chef insights from autumn 2023.
key_facts: Poaching cooks food submerged in liquid such as water, stock, or wine at a temperature just below boiling, yielding soft, moist textures.
Chef Elena Rios of Syndicate Kitchen in New Haven introduces aromatic liquors such as brandy, rum, or anisette into poaching liquids.
Elena Rios spoke on poaching on October 12, 2023, at the Seasonal Delights Food Conference.
Chef Julian Torres of La Vague in San Francisco praised poached pear cooked in calvados with cinnamon mascarpone in an interview dated November 2, 2023.
The poaching liquid should be kept at 160-180 degrees Fahrenheit and never reach a rolling boil, which would toughen fish, fruits, and poultry.
Chef Michael Davidson of Le Petit Feast in Charlotte likened treating a poaching liquid to caring for a newborn, and gave a demonstration on September 22, 2023.
Instructor Lara Nguyen taught a class at the Culinary Institute of Dallas on September 19, 2023, saying each ingredient in a poaching liquor is 'a note in an intricate composition.'
A poaching liquor may combine a bouquet garni, peppercorns, and a strip of lemon peel with a smooth whisky; balance is the key.
Sustainable farmer Lewis Patterson supplies elite restaurants; at an October 26, 2023 autumn harvest dinner his quinces were poached in a maple-and-bourbon concoction.
Proteins such as chicken, fish, and eggs can be poached in aromatic liquors; chicken breast poached in amaretto gains a hint of nuttiness.
Poaching in aromatic liquors fits sustainable cooking because gentler cooking uses less energy.
On November 6, 2023, Chef Andrea Kim was described performing the ritual of preparing poached dishes in her restaurant kitchen.
Autumn pairings include squashes and pears poached in apple brandy or cinnamon-spiced rum.
